about: Pronunciation profiles for the trope engine's text front end (trope/text.mjs). One profile per reading tradition; verseUnits() takes { pronunciation: <profile name> | <profile object> }. Rationale and the open questions for the cantor: docs/superpowers/research/2026-10-15-trope-engine/hebrew-text-pipeline.md sections 2-4. Symbols are engine-internal ASCII names (the DiffSinger 'he/<name>' column of section 4 without the prefix, except yod = j); the symbols table gives IPA, X-SAMPA and an ARPAbet-ish fallback for each. An empty string means 'no phoneme'.

israeli-v1.name: israeli-v1
israeli-v1.description: Modern Israeli ('Sephardic-style') reading as used in American non-Orthodox congregations. Tiberian syllable structure (vocal sheva, hataf vowels and dagesh forte all kept), Israeli segment values. Not yet confirmed with Cantor Finkel.

syllabifier.about: Options passed to havarotjs' Text(). longVowels: true is the Tiberian rule (a sheva after a long vowel is vocal: u-vei-ne-CHA); set false for the Israeli habit (u-vein-CHA). qametsQatan is false because MAM already marks every qamats qatan with U+05C7; letting havarotjs guess could only add errors.

consonants.about: Letter -> phoneme. { dagesh, plain } where the letter's sound changes with dagesh lene/forte (BeGaDKeFaT); a string otherwise. Shin/sin are told apart by their dots. Alef and ayin are not here: rules.alefOnset and rules.ayin decide them, and silent letters (quiescent alef, mater he/vav/yod) never reach this table.

vowels.about: havarotjs vowel name -> phoneme. SHEVA is the vocal sheva (sheva na); a silent sheva is never looked up. Hataf vowels are sung as their own short syllable.

rules.tsereYodAbout: Yod after tsere or segol with no vowel of its own: 'e' (silent yod, be-NI) or 'ej' (bei-NI, adds a j).
rules.geminateAbout: Dagesh forte: 'double' gives the consonant twice (coda of one syllable + onset of the next: yip-pa-KED); 'single' gives it once, as onset only.
rules.qamatsYodShevaAbout: Yod with sheva after an open qamats syllable without meteg (הַלָּ֑יְלָה): "nach" closes the syllable (ha-LAY-la); "na" keeps havarotjs longVowels reading (ha-LA-ye-la).
rules.furtiveAbout: Furtive patach (final ח/ע/הּ after a non-a vowel): the vowel is sounded before the consonant, as its own unstressed syllable (ga-VO-ah).
rules.alefOnsetAbout: Alef that carries a vowel: '' (no onset, the Israeli norm) or 'q' (glottal stop). Alef with no vowel is always silent.
rules.ayinAbout: Ayin: '' (none, merged with alef) or 'q' (glottal stop).
rules.divineNameAbout: The Tetragrammaton is sung as the pointed word given here; the Elohim pointing (hataf segol first or hiriq last) reads elohim.
